{"analyses":[{"paper_id":"doi-10-1007-978-3-319-67684-5-24","title":"RemindMe: Plugging a Reminder Manager into Email for Enhancing Workplace Responsiveness","research_question":"Can a reminder-management layer integrated with enterprise email reduce the cognitive burden of tracking incoming and outgoing workplace requests and improve reminder handling over time?","methodology":"The paper presents the design of RemindMe, drawing on prior research in social request management, interruption management, prospective memory, and cognitive psychology. The system combines an email-reminder creation algorithm with a learning mechanism intended to improve reminders over time and a user interface for reminder delivery. application.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Abstract"},{"finding":"The browser-plugin architecture allows the reminder functionality to be added on top of an existing enterprise webmail extraction?","methodology":"CLIN-SUMM incrementally builds categorized, date-partitioned patient representations, using separate prompts for initial summarization and subsequent change-focused facts, numbers and science","research_question":"How should epistemic uncertainty about facts, numerical quantities, and scientific hypotheses be classified and expressed, and what does existing Discussion"},{"finding":"Communicators should distinguish the magnitude of an effect or claim from the strength or certainty of the evidence supporting expression was found in real-world use.","Uncertainty communication can affect cognition, emotion, trust, and behavior.","The literature does not show that communicating uncertainty inevitably communication."],"source_url":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6549952/","access":"full_text"},{"paper_id":"manual-1d6b22c7ad","title":"Corpus-Based Problem Selection for EHR Note Summarization","research_question":"Can corpus-derived lexical, frequency, persistence, and temporal features identify which clinical problems from longitudinal notes should be retained in a concise patient summary?","methodology":"The authors formulate problem selection as binary classification after using MedLEE and UMLS/SNOMED resources to identify candidate clinical problems in notes. They train primarily on a renal outpatient corpus of 1,618 patients averaging 14.3 notes per patient, using the final past-medical-history section as a scalable surrogate for summary-relevant problems, and separately evaluate against nephrologist-authored summaries for four patients. Naive Bayes and C4.5 classifiers, multiple feature-selection schemes, section restrictions, concept grouping, and negation filtering are evaluated with precision, recall, F-measure, F2, error rates, and confidence intervals.","key_findings":[{"finding":"The best reported relevance-classification accuracy reached 82%, with an F-measure of selection.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Input Section Analysis"},{"finding":"A simple filter for problems that were predominantly or finally negated improved both precision and recall in the reported experiments.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Filtering Negated Findings"},{"finding":"When precision and recall were weighted equally, best-first feature selection helped remove extraneous problems from the proposed summary.","evidence_type":"supported","section":"Overall Evaluation"},{"finding":"When recall was weighted more heavily through F2, omitting feature selection narrative."],"reproducibility":{"code_available":false,"dataset_available":false,"metrics_reported":true},"confidence_scores":{"peak_accuracy_and_fmeasure":0.99,"section_restriction_hurts":0.99,"negation_filter_improves":0.99,"best_first_precision_recall_tradeoff":0.98,"f2_prefers_no_feature_selection":0.98,"note_features_outperform_temporal":0.97,"coding_granularity_problem":0.99},"raw_claims":["The
